summary: Reproduced the reviewed idle-prefix failure at candidate 7fe1b5433ded03af468fe10969159eae92792666 and moved retract invalidation to scheduler scope, using a complete cache reset and allocator clear so finished-request prefixes and hierarchical backing state are invalidated. The documented live disaggregated-prefill mid-chunk exception remains.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact candidate failing-before: a completed-request four-token RadixCache prefix remained 4/4 matchable after an idle retract pause.

Passing-after scheduler/cache behavior: 37 tests and 2 subtests passed, including the unchanged independent idle counterexample, full reset boundary, hierarchical reset-not-evict assertion, and retained disaggregated-prefill boundary.
The assigned AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950 was visible and returned 3.0 for a simple device sum; this was environment evidence, not a model reproduction.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-b93267b61db1/evidence/gpu-inventory.txt records one AMD Instinct MI355X, capability (9, 5), and a successful device sum. Issue-specific tests executed on CPU.
remaining_limitations: A live mid-chunk request in disaggregated-prefill mode is deliberately retained because freeing its KV while the disaggregated sender is live is unsafe; stale-weight KV remains possible in that documented path until sender teardown is implemented.
The reported Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 weights were unavailable, so no full-model weight-swap, logprob, or generated-text reproduction was performed.
No hierarchical-cache runtime fixture was available; the hierarchical correction is supported by source behavior and a scheduler boundary regression asserting reset rather than generic eviction.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
